script: A delivery truck has reached the main gate. Where should the driver wait before entering?
Where should the driver park first?
Park in the waiting area, switch off the engine, and walk to Security.
Wait in the waiting area with the engine off. Do not drive straight inside.
The driver has five documents. Match each one to the right desk.
Sort each incoming document to the correct reception desk:
Security checks driver and vehicle documents. The Data Entry Operator checks shipping papers and prepares the gate pass.
Send Purchase Order, Advanced Shipping Notice, and invoice to the Data Entry Operator. Send the driver's license and vehicle papers to Security.
The Data Entry Operator enters the invoice in the system. The system checks whether the truck delivery matches the Advanced Shipping Notice.
What does this system check do if the Advanced Shipping Notice is wrong?
The system fills the shipment details from the Advanced Shipping Notice. If it does not match, stop the gate entry until it is corrected.
Do not proceed with mismatched data. Stop the gate entry until the Advanced Shipping Notice is corrected.
The Data Entry Operator issues the gate entry pass! The printer prints the barcode pass while the driver checks the status display. Put the gate entry steps in the correct order.
Arrange the driver's gate entry journey in the correct chronological order:
Spot on! The correct flow is: park truck, security check, system check, get barcode pass, then move to dock. This prevents gate congestion and ensures 100% record tracking.
Stop! The driver cannot move to the dock before getting the printed barcode pass. Let us arrange the steps in the correct order.
The Data Entry Operator assigns the warehouse dock! Based on our shipment of vehicle mechanical parts, which warehouse dock on the AURIC plant layout must be allocated?
The Data Entry Operator assigns the warehouse dock for vehicle assembly parts. Tap the correct allocated bay & dock on the AURIC plant layout:
Spot on! Dock 04 in Inbound Bay B is designated for vehicle assembly components. Dock 01 is reserved for battery cells and Dock 06 for hazardous chemicals.
Careful! Dock 01 is an environmentally controlled vault for battery cells only, and Dock 06 is for chemicals. Vehicle parts belong at Dock 04.
The truck is docked at Bay B, Dock 04! Before keys and invoices are handed over and unloading begins, inspect the vehicle for a critical safety violation.
Spot the immediate safety violation before keys are accepted and unloading starts:
Lifesaving catch! Heavy rubber wheel chocks must be placed under rear tires to prevent trailer roll-away when forklifts enter.
High danger alert! If a 3-ton forklift drives inside an unchocked trailer, trailer creep will cause the forklift to plunge into the dock gap!

Unloading is done! The truck has loaded 20 empty blue Foldable Large Container bins to return to the vendor. At the exit gate, the driver demands: 'Open the boom barrier, these are just Ather's empty bins!' What must you do?
The driver wants to leave with 20 empty Foldable Large Container bins without a manual Delivery Challan:
Brilliant vigilance! Returnable bins require an authorized manual Delivery Challan and system exit clearance before the exit gate barrier opens!
Stop! Never raise the barrier without a manual Delivery Challan. Empty bins are valuable Ather company assets. Without a Delivery Challan, thousands of rupees of packaging exit untracked!

Attention Data Entry Operator! The driver presents an invoice for 50 battery harnesses, but the digital Advanced Shipping Notice in SAP ERP shows only 40 units for this Purchase Order line! Can you issue a gate entry pass?
The physical invoice quantity differs from the digital Advanced Shipping Notice in SAP:

Right call! Never create a gate pass for a mismatched shipment. The Data Entry Operator halts the transaction and alerts the Inbound Gate Incharge within 1 hour to resolve the vendor Advanced Shipping Notice discrepancy.
Violation! Generating a gate pass with an incorrect Advanced Shipping Notice creates major inventory mismatches in SAP ERP that block quality inspection receiving and vendor payment clearance.

A scheduled chassis frame truck reports at Gate 01. However, the SAP inventory screen indicates that High-Rise Rack storage for frames is already at 100% maximum capacity! What is the mandatory Data Entry Operator action?
The maximum stock capacity for this material is full in the warehouse. What must the Data Entry Operator do?

Spot-on! The truck remains in the designated waiting parking area until line assembly consumes existing stock and clears warehouse pallet positions. Dumping material on dock gangways is strictly forbidden.
Incorrect! Never dump material in active dock corridors or send the supplier away. Truck must wait in parking bay until pallet locations clear.

Welcome to Stage 2: Receiving & quality inspection Clearance! The forklift has offloaded a pallet of brake calipers at Dock 04 Inbound Staging. Look closely at the freshly pasted Goods Receipt Note sticker on the pallet. What does that large '?' symbol tell us?
Forklifts have offloaded the pallet into Inbound Staging. You inspect the freshly pasted Goods Receipt Note sticker and spot a large '?' printed on it. What does this symbol mean?
Spot on! A '?' on the Goods Receipt Note sticker designates Non-Direct-on-Line material. It requires mandatory 10% sampling and testing by quality inspection before it can be put away into storage!

Hold on! A '?' symbol does not mean scrap or direct-to-line. It means Non-Direct-on-Line—the material must undergo mandatory quality inspection sampling. Premature put-away of uninspected stock will be blocked by SAP warehouse management system!

Now that we know the shipment is Non-Direct-on-Line, we must apply the 10% statistical sampling rule! The Purchase Order contains 10 Foldable Large Container crates (100 total brake calipers). Exactly how many Foldable Large Container crates must be separated and transferred to the quality inspection testing area?
A Non-Direct-on-Line lot of 10 Foldable Large Containers has arrived. following the standard 10% statistical sampling rule, how many Foldable Large Container crates must go to quality inspection?
Precise math! 10% of 10 Foldable Large Containers is exactly 1 crate (10 calipers). Moving only 1 crate prevents testing bottleneck while ensuring batch quality.

Calculation error! Exactly 10% of the inward volume must be sampled. For a 10-Foldable Large Container lot, sending more than 1 crate congests the quality inspection lab; sending less violates standard rules.

1 sample crate has gone to the testing lab, but 9 brake caliper crates remain in Receiving Inbound Staging. What physical indicator cone must be placed on these 9 crates to warn forklift operators not to touch them?
The 9 remaining FLC crates are waiting in staging during the 2-hour quality testing window. What visual safety marker must you place around them?
Excellent safety awareness! A Yellow Cone clearly marks stock waiting for quality inspection. Forklift drivers must never move pallets marked with yellow cones.
Danger of part mix-up! Never leave uninspected crates without a cone, and never put a green cone before final quality pass. Always place the yellow Under quality inspection cone.
Goods Receipt Note sticker pasted and 10% sample pallet separated! What is the maximum allowed time SLA to physically hand over this sample crate to the quality inspection lab?
Following Goods Receipt Note label application, what is the strict SLA cutoff time for inbound manpower to hand over Non-Direct-on-Line samples to the quality inspection testing room?
Right on time! The handover must happen within 30 minutes. Exceeding this delays inspection and bottlenecks subsequent dock put-away.
SLA overrun! Waiting longer than 30 minutes violates handover rules, causing dock congestion and blocking incoming vehicle parts.

The quality inspection inspector has finished testing the sample! The incoming lot will receive one of 3 distinct outcomes: Pass, Hold, or NG (Not Good / Reject). Match each physical cone to its correct status.
Match the Incoming Quality Control (quality inspection) outcome to the mandatory physical warehouse action:
Flawless matching! Green Cone means Pass (put away to racks), Red Cone means NG/Reject (move to Quarantine), and Yellow Cone with tag means Hold (awaiting engineering decision).
Mismatch! Green is Pass, Red is NG/Reject, and Yellow is Under quality inspection / Hold. Misplacing cones risks putting defective stock into production!
Welcome to the quality inspection gate! Every inbound shipment unloaded at Dock 04 is categorized into Direct-on-Line or Non-Direct-on-Line. How do these two material categories differ?
What does quality inspection stand for, and what is its primary purpose at Ather AURIC?
Clear understanding! Direct-on-Line parts from certified suppliers go straight to storage or line without sampling. Non-Direct-on-Line parts must undergo mandatory quality inspection testing.
Misunderstanding! Direct-on-Line is not uninspected forever; it relies on trusted supplier quality certificates. Non-Direct-on-Line requires sampling at Ather before use.
During a new factory launch or supplier ramp-up, Ather enforces an exception rule: even certified Direct-on-Line parts must temporarily undergo 100% receiving inspection. Why?
In a new factory, during the first 6 months, which inward parts must go to quality inspection?
Quality vigilance! During ramp-up, processes are stabilizing. 100% inspection catches tooling deviations early and prevents flawed parts from entering production.
Risk blind spot! Trusting unverified new production lines risks catastrophic assembly defects. Ramp-up requires temporary 100% inspection gatekeeping.
Mastering the receiving sequence is essential! Put the complete workflow for Non-Direct-on-Line material in the correct chronological order.
Put the Non-Direct-on-Line Receiving and quality inspection steps in correct chronological order:
Excellent! Unload and paste Goods Receipt Note label, sample 10% and place Under quality inspection cone, hand over to lab within 30 minutes, then receive the final Pass, Hold, or NG decision.
Wrong sequence! First paste the Goods Receipt Note label before sampling, and mark the 10% sample crates with cones before handing them over to the lab.

Non-Direct-on-Line sample crates have been sitting in receiving staging for 75 minutes because the team was busy offloading another truck! What is the critical systemic risk of exceeding the 30-minute handover SLA?
Non-Direct-on-Line samples are not issued to quality inspection within the 30-minute SLA. What is the operational risk?
Spot-on! If samples are not issued within 30 minutes, the open SAP warehouse order stays locked. This blocks put-away for upcoming shipments and halts parts supply to the assembly line.
Violation! Delayed quality inspection handover deadlocks the SAP warehouse management system queue. Inbound Zone Leader must immediately prioritize sample delivery to clear the system block.

Welcome to Stage 3: Vehicle & Battery Parts Put-Away! The incoming brake caliper lot has passed inspection and carries the green 'QC Pass' seal. An Material Handling Equipment reach-truck operator arrives with a rugged handheld terminal. Before moving any pallet toward the racks, what mandatory digital scan must be performed to initiate the SAP warehouse management system Warehouse Task?
In Goods Receipt Note staging, what must the Material Handling Equipment operator scan first with the rugged handheld terminal to generate the Put-Away Warehouse Task?

Standard procedure verified! The operator must scan the pallet-level Handling Unit barcode on the Goods Receipt Note sticker first. Scanning the Handling Unit instructs SAP warehouse management system to generate the Warehouse Task, displaying the target High-Rise Rack bin and part specifications!

Incorrect scan sequence! You cannot begin put-away without scanning the Handling Unit label first. Moving material before the Handling Unit scan leaves SAP warehouse management system blind to pallet movement, causing open task backlogs and ERP stock mismatch.

The Handling Unit has been scanned and the warehouse task is active! The forklift reaches a major internal junction with two paths. Inbound parts arrive in two packaging forms: standard blue FLC crates and wheeled body trolleys. How must these two material streams be separated?
How should FLC crates and body trolleys be separated at the junction?
Spot on! Standard FLC crates go to High-Rise Racks using reach-trucks. Wheeled body trolleys go directly to ground-level Trolley Staging lanes.

Route routing error! Wheeled trolleys cannot be placed on High-Rise Racks due to beam clearance and weight distribution hazards, and Foldable Large Container pallets cannot block the floor-level trolley feeding lanes!

The reach-truck places the Foldable Large Container crate at High-Rise Rack Aisle B, Level 2, Bin 12! To finalize the digital bin marriage in SAP warehouse management system, what final scan must the operator execute?
The Foldable Large Container pallet is resting on shelf Rack Beam B-04. What mandatory action must the operator execute to formally conclude the put-away?

Flawless execution! Scanning the physical QR code on the rack beam creates the digital bin marriage in SAP warehouse management system, confirms the Warehouse Task, and marks the inventory as available stock!

Incomplete task! Moving the pallet into the rack is not enough. Without scanning the beam QR code, SAP warehouse management system cannot verify the bin marriage, leaving the task hanging and the stock unavailable!

Warning! A trainee operator lifted 100 brake calipers, placed them into High-Rise Rack bin HRR-B-04-12, but drove away without scanning the rack location QR code! What serious warehouse defect does this cause?
An Material Handling Equipment operator placed an Foldable Large Container pallet into the rack but forgot to scan the destination location QR code before driving away. What happens?

Critical insight! Because the destination scan was skipped, SAP warehouse management system leaves the Warehouse Task open. The stock shows as missing in the system, risking line-stoppage even though parts are physically in the rack!
Major oversight! Leaving a task open creates a ghost stockout. The operator must return and complete the destination scan immediately.

Aisle 04 alert! Your scanner screen directs you to high bin A-02 on Level 2. But the lower bin B-03 right next to you is empty, and the operator considers placing the pallet in Bin B to save time. Should this be permitted?
The SAP handheld displays assigned Bin A, but the operator places the pallet into Bin B to save time. What must be done?

STOP IS THE ONLY CORRECT ACTION! The system strictly dictates storage bins based on First-In First-Out, part weight, and pick frequency algorithms. Putting stock in an unassigned bin creates severe inventory discrepancies. The system will NOT close the Warehouse Task unless the assigned bin is scanned. You must either move it to Bin A or request the Zone Leader to re-slot in SAP warehouse management system!

CRITICAL STORAGE MISMATCH! Placing pallets in unassigned bins causes 'ghost stockouts' during assembly line picking. The system will flag an open task against your ID and picking operators will find an empty bin!

Final Put-Away certification milestone! You have mastered the rules of handling units, high-rise racks, bin marriage, and error recovery. Now prove your operational mastery by arranging the complete put-away lifecycle in its exact chronological order!
Arrange the 5 mandatory put-away steps in the exact operational sequence

OUTSTANDING ACCURACY! You have successfully mastered the official sequence: First, Paste Goods Receipt Note label, Second, Scan Handling Unit label, Third, Carry pallet to the location, Fourth, Scan location QR code, Task closes and SAP stock updates! Stage 3: Vehicle & Battery Parts Put-Away is 100% complete!

Incorrect sequence! Remember The Goods Receipt Note label must be pasted first, followed by scanning the Handling Unit to initiate the task, transporting to the bin, scanning the rack QR, and finally system closure!

Welcome to Stage 4: Specialized Battery Cell Put-Away! High-value lithium-ion battery cell crates have arrived at Dock 01. These sensitive cells power the Ather 450X and are hazardous if mishandled. A general warehouse helper grabs a manual pallet truck to move the pallet to clear the dock floor. Should they proceed?
A general warehouse helper attempts to move an unloaded lithium-ion battery cell pallet using a manual Hand Pallet Truck to clear the dock floor. Allow or halt this transfer?

STOP IS CORRECT! Battery cells must be handled and transported EXCLUSIVELY by certified Material Handling Equipment operators using designated electric reach-trucks or powered pallet trucks. Uncertified handling risks thermal shocks, mechanical puncture, or dangerous cell dropping!

CRITICAL SAFETY VIOLATION! General warehouse associates and manual helpers are strictly prohibited from moving lithium-ion cell shipments. Mishandling fragile battery cells can cause internal short circuits, fire hazards, and complete warranty voiding.

The forklift operator has moved the lithium-ion cell pallet through the airlock into the Battery Standard Room. Before placing the pallet into the cell vault, check the room monitors. What are the strict temperature and humidity limits required by SOP?
Under Ather AURIC what are the mandatory environmental thresholds for the Battery Cell Standard Room?

Exactly right! The Battery Standard Room must stay between 20°C and 25°C with 60% to 65% humidity 24/7. This protects battery cells from overheating, moisture absorption, and internal chemical damage!
Environmental limits violated! Temperatures above 25°C damage battery life, while humidity outside 60% to 65% creates moisture and static spark risks near sensitive battery terminals.

Pay close attention to the warehouse clock! Lithium-ion battery cell pallets cannot sit idling on the inbound dock or open air corridors due to ambient temperature shifts. What is the mandatory time limit from dock unloading to climate-controlled room transfer?
Under Ather AURIC what is the mandatory maximum SLA window for completing battery cell put-away from Goods Receipt Note staging into the standard room?

Clockwork discipline! Battery pallets must reach the climate-controlled Battery Standard Room within 60 minutes of dock unloading. Prompt transfer protects cell electrochemistry and warranty certification.
Time limit exceeded! Leaving lithium-ion cells in dock heat for over 1 hour damages battery life and cancels supplier warranty.

ALARM ALERT! As you prepare to store cells in the vault, the wall display flashes amber: Humidity has jumped to 75.2% and temperature is rising to 27.4°C. High moisture destroys battery cells! What is your immediate action?
While moving lithium-ion cells into the Standard Room, the wall display flashes amber: Humidity has spiked to 75% (Limit: 60%–65%). What must you do immediately?

PERFECT EMERGENCY RESPONSE! When room conditions go out of limit, immediately stop moving the pallet, close airlock doors to seal the room, and inform the Putaway Zone Leader and HVAC team. Never store cells in an out-of-spec vault!

CATASTROPHIC CONTAMINATION RISK! Never ignore an active environmental breach or attempt to bypass humidity trips. 75% RH triggers moisture condensation on lithium-ion terminals, creating hazardous internal micro-shorts and battery fires. Halt, isolate, and escalate immediately!
An operator sees two battery cell crates already stacked on a pallet. Another worker tries to stack a third crate on top to save floor space. What must you do?
An operator attempts to stack battery cell crates 3-high on a storage pallet despite a triggered red ShockWatch impact indicator on the carton. Allow or halt?

STOP IS STRICTLY REQUIRED! Battery cell crates must never be stacked more than 2 high to prevent crushing and internal short circuits. If a ShockWatch or tilt sensor turns red, immediately move the pallet to quarantine and alert Quality! Module 4 is now 100% complete!

CRITICAL SAFETY HAZARD! Stacking 3 crates high crushes fragile lithium-ion pouches, risking electrolyte leakage and internal short-circuit fire. A red shock indicator means the shipment suffered severe impact during transit and cannot enter active assembly stock!

Welcome to Stage 5: Hazardous Chemicals & Thinners Put-Away! A supplier truck carrying drums of flammable thinners, paints, and hazardous solvents arrives at the AURIC Main Gate. The driver asks if they should dock at Inbound Dock 01 (Main Assembly Building) with the other standard trucks. Under Ather where must chemical and thinner shipments proceed?
A delivery truck arrives with drums of combustible thinners and industrial paints. The driver asks to unload at Dock 01 next to vehicle body panels. Where does Ather mandate this vehicle proceed?

PERFECT FACILITY BYPASS ROUTING! Hazardous chemicals, thinners, and paints are stored in separate, designated buildings. The gate pass specifies the exact isolated building. Trucks must bypass the main assembly plant completely and dock directly at the detached Chemical Storage detached Chemical Annex, equipped with flameproof fixtures and spill berms!

CRITICAL INDUSTRIAL FIRE HAZARD! Hazardous solvents, combustible paints, and thinners must NEVER enter the main manufacturing plant or general Dock 01. Vapors or accidental leaks near high-voltage assembly lines create catastrophic explosion risks!

At Chemical Storage Annex, the truck has docked and an operator begins unloading 200-liter steel drums of industrial thinner. Take a close look at the unloading setup. Under Ather which critical safety hazard violates our mandatory chemical handling protocols?
Spot the Safety Violation: An operator is unloading 200L flammable thinner drums at Chemical Storage Annex. Which condition violates Ather safety protocols?

HAZARD SPOTTED! Never place flammable liquids on bare concrete without a spill tray, and always attach the earthing clamp to steel drums before handling. A static spark can instantly ignite thinner vapors into a fire, and leaks can cause serious chemical contamination!

CRITICAL SAFETY RISK OVERLOOKED! Staging flammable solvent drums directly on bare concrete with disconnected grounding earthing wires is an extreme industrial hazard. A single static discharge spark can ignite the entire chemical warehouse!

Chemical Storage Annex holds two distinct chemical categories: Class 3 Flammable Solvents and Class 8 Corrosive Battery Electrolytes. How must these two chemical classes be stored inside the facility?
Segregate incoming chemicals into their designated storage bays according to Ather 2-Hour SLA limit:

FLAWLESS CHEMICAL SEPARATION! Flammables and acids must be stored in separate storage bays with their own spill trays. If solvent vapors mix with acid fumes, they can cause dangerous chemical reactions, toxic smoke, and explosions!

DANGEROUS MIXING HAZARD! Storing flammable solvents in the same tray or bay as battery acids creates extreme fire and explosion hazards. Incompatible chemicals must always be stored in separate bays with dedicated spill trays!

At Chemical Storage Annex, the put-away operator has successfully unloaded, inspected, and segregated 20 drums of industrial thinner into Bay 1. Who is responsible under Ather for generating the official Goods Receipt Note in SAP and posting the inventory stock into the ERP system?
After a chemical delivery truck is unloaded and physically verified at the Chemical Storage Annex, who is responsible for creating the Goods Receipt Note in SAP?

EXACT ROLE HANDOVER! The put-away operator unloads and checks the physical material. Once verified, the Data Entry Operator creates the Goods Receipt Note, pastes labels, and posts stock into SAP once putting away is complete!

ROLE CONFUSION HAZARD! Put-away operators handle physical material movement, earthing, and putting away stock, but they do not create the Goods Receipt Note. The Data Entry Operator creates the GRN and posts inventory into SAP.

Urgent safety check at Chemical Storage! A 200-liter drum of thinner sits on a spill pallet. Before opening the drum cap for a QC sample, an operator grabs a steel wrench without attaching the earthing clamp to ground. He says: 'It will only take 10 seconds.' Should you allow this or stop it immediately?
An operator is about to open a 200-liter solvent drum cap for QC sampling without attaching the earthing clamp. Allow or stop?

STOPPING IT IS THE ONLY SAFE DECISION! A static spark from tool friction or liquid movement can trigger an instant fireball! You must firmly attach earthing clamps to clean metal before touching or opening any chemical drum. Module 5 is now 100% complete!

SERIOUS FIRE HAZARD! Invisible solvent vapors gather around chemical drum caps. A spark without earthing can cause an instant explosion and plant evacuation! Never loosen a drum cap without attaching the earthing clamp!

Welcome to Stage 6: Supermarket C-Class Parts Put-Away! Small fasteners and grommets have arrived at the Material Handling staging desk from inbound receiving. The lot is marked Non-Direct-on-Line, but looking closely at the Goods Receipt Note sticker, the green 'QC Pass' circular stamp is completely missing! The line is waiting for these screws. Should the operator proceed to put these into the supermarket racks?

A Non-Direct-on-Line lot of small fasteners arrives at the supermarket receiving desk. The Goods Receipt Note sticker has no green 'QC Pass' seal attached. Allow or halt put-away into supermarket racks?

STOP IS THE CORRECT DECISION! For Non-Direct-on-Line parts, the physical 'QC Pass' seal or sticker is mandatory on the Goods Receipt Note label. Without this seal, the parts have NOT been released by Quality Control and could be defective. Moving uncertified parts to the supermarket risks line assembly defects and immediate vehicle recalls!

CRITICAL QUALITY BREACH! No associate may move a Non-Direct-on-Line lot to supermarket bins without a verified green 'QC Pass' stamp. Skipping inspection risks assembling loose fasteners into vehicles, causing catastrophic field breakdowns!

At the receiving desk, you print the SAP inventory dump from the system, which shows expected stock of 100 M6 hex bolts. You perform a sample count on the digital counting scale and find only 92 pieces—an 8-piece shortage! A line feeder says: 'Just put the 92 bolts into the bin so the line doesn't stop, and adjust the number later.' What is the mandatory action under Ather?
The SAP stock report indicates 100 pieces for an inward C-class lot, but physical sampling at Material Handling reveals only 92 pieces. What must the operator do?

STANDARD PROCEDURE ENFORCED! If any discrepancy exists between the physical count and the SAP dump, the operator must IMMEDIATELY halt put-away for that material and escalate to the Supermarket Zone Leader. Never alter slips or stock short lots, as this creates ghost inventory that starves future production!

CRITICAL INVENTORY ERROR! Changing numbers or stocking short parts without telling your Zone Leader ruins SAP stock accuracy. The next shift will expect 100 bolts, and assembly will suddenly stop when only 92 are there!

Count audits are cleared! Now we proceed to the supermarket gravity flow racks. These roller tracks operate on strict First-In First-Out. You must ALWAYS load from the REAR loading lane so boxes glide forward to the front picking face. Loading from the front traps older parts behind. Arrange the 4 put-away steps in the correct order!
Arrange the 4 steps of Gravity Flow Rack put-away in the correct sequence to ensure FIFO stock rotation:
Spot on! Loading from the rear maintains First-In First-Out flow and ensures assembly workers always pick the oldest verified stock first.
Incorrect! Never load boxes from the front picking face. Loading from the front violates First-In First-Out and traps aging inventory.

Look at the front of the supermarket rack! After line kitters picked parts, stock hit the red MIN level (only 2 boxes left). What two actions must you take immediately to prevent the assembly line from running out?
The fastener bin has reached its safety minimum stock level of 2 boxes (200 pieces). What must the Supermarket operator execute immediately?
Spot on! Scan the Kanban replenishment barcode to trigger a restock task in the system, and notify the Supermarket Zone Leader immediately.
Warning! Do not wait until the bin is completely empty. When stock reaches the red MIN line, trigger replenishment immediately.

EXTREME PRESSURE AT THE SUPERMARKET RECEIVING DESK! You counted 92 bolts instead of 100 on the counting scale. A line feeder rushes in, yelling that the Main Frame assembly line will shut down in 2 minutes! They demand: 'Sign off on all 100 pieces right now, hand me the bin, and we will reconcile the missing 8 parts later.' Do you permit this dispatch or execute a hard stop?
Physical count is 92 pcs (SAP expected: 100 pcs). Under urgent line-stoppage pressure, the line feeder demands you sign off 100 pcs immediately. Allow or Halt?

STOP IS STRICTLY REQUIRED! Never sign false counts or release unverified quantities under line pressure! Any count mismatch means stop and alert your Supermarket Zone Leader. Fake counts create missing stock and cause serious billing disputes!
SERIOUS INVENTORY ERROR! Giving in to line pressure and entering 100 pieces when only 92 arrived ruins SAP inventory records. The next shift will run out of bolts and shut down the assembly line!
Final Supermarket certification question! Which parts are authorized to be stored in Supermarket flow racks at Ather AURIC plant?
Which categories of parts are stored in Supermarket racks at the Ather AURIC Plant?

PERFECT CLASSIFICATION MASTERY! Supermarket racks are designated EXCLUSIVELY for small C-class items (screws, bolts, clips, washers, O-rings) that are verified at the receiving desk first. Heavy A-class parts belong to High-Rise Racks and Trolley Staging! Stage 6: Supermarket C-Class Parts Put-Away is 100% complete!

INCORRECT CLASSIFICATION! Supermarket gravity racks cannot hold heavy A-class frames or flammable chemicals. Supermarket racks are strictly dedicated to small C-class hardware parts checked at the receiving desk!

Critical quality alert at quality inspection Test Bench 02! While inspecting a 10-piece sample from an incoming batch of 1,000 battery harness connectors, the inspector discovers 2 burnt, defective terminals with critical high resistance. Which parts must be sent to the NG Quarantine area immediately?
When quality inspection finds 2 defective burnt connectors in a 10-piece sample from a 1,000-piece lot, what materials must be moved to the NG Quarantine area?

Spot on! In statistical sampling, even a single defect rejects the entire batch. All 1,000 harness connectors must be sent to the Quarantine cage immediately. Never segregate just the defective samples and pass the rest!
Critical error! Never pick out only the defective pieces and pass the rest of the lot. When sample testing fails, the entire batch must be quarantined immediately!
You inspect the pallet: it has a physical Red Tag, but the JIRA ticket is still pending. Can you move this material into the quarantine cage?
A rejected lot carries a Red Tag, but the QC sticker is missing and the JIRA ticket has no Bug ID ('Unknown Cause'). Can the NG team collect it?

ABSOLUTELY STOP! For Rejected Return to Vendor every rejected part MUST have BOTH a Red Tag AND a QC sticker, plus a JIRA ticket with a valid Bug ID! Collecting untracked parts creates ghost inventory and voids supplier warranty debit notes!
Critical hazard! Never move rejected stock without dual physical identification (Red Tag + QC sticker) and an active JIRA Bug ID. Doing so causes untraceable inventory in the quarantine cage!

We have entered the high-security caged Quarantine Store! As rejected materials are stored here, SAP moves inventory to 'Blocked Stock'. Why is physical and digital quarantine separation strictly enforced?
Drag each rejected lot to its correct storage bay inside the Quarantine Cage based on its defect cause:
Spot on! Parts inside the Quarantine Store must be segregated by root cause and vendor into designated bays (Supplier Quality, In-House Transit Damage, and Rework) to prevent mix-ups.
Incorrect! Never dump all rejected parts together in a single pile. They must be strictly segregated by root cause into marked quarantine bays.

The Material Review Board—team members from Quality, Production, and Warehouse—meets in Quarantine to decide what to do with 4 quarantined lots. Verbal approvals are never allowed! Match each quarantined lot to its approved action: Return to Vendor, Rework, Use As-Is, or Scrap.
Sort the 4 quarantined material cases into their approved action routes
PERFECT DISPOSITION ROUTING! Critical dimension failure returns to vendor; minor harness scratches get reworked; minor cosmetic sticker tilt is used as-is; cracked structural casting is scrapped!
Quality rule violation! Never mix up actions for damaged stock. Damaged structural parts cannot be accepted under deviation, and vendor manufacturing defects must be returned for credit!

We have reached the Ather Scrap Yard and outbound weighbridge. Scrapped parts must be crushed in an industrial shredder so they can never re-enter the market, then the truck is weighed before leaving. Put the 4 scrap disposal steps in the correct order!
Arrange the 4 steps of Scrap and Vendor Weighbridge Exit in the correct sequence:

Outstanding precision! First, Finance and Production sign-off; Second, shredding of parts so branded components cannot enter grey markets; Third, JIRA photo upload for audit; Fourth, weighbridge dual-weighting (empty vs full) before final Delivery Challan release.
Severe audit breach! Never dispatch scrap before physical destruction and dual weighbridge logging. Doing so creates scrap theft risks!

Visual floor controls at Dock 02! An incoming lot of motor mount brackets has been delayed at the inspection station because specialized CMM measuring equipment is undergoing morning calibration. The pallet must sit in the staging area for 3 hours. Which visual cone must you place on this waiting pallet?
quality inspection inspection is delayed and an inward lot is waiting in staging. Which cone do you place on the pallet?

PERFECT IDENTIFICATION! When an incoming lot is delayed in inspection, place the Yellow 'IQC Hold' cone. 'Hold' means waiting for quality decision—not defective. The Red 'NG' cone is only for parts that failed quality inspection!

INCORRECT CONE PLACEMENT! Placing an 'NG' cone on a lot that simply has delayed testing causes false vendor panic, wrongful debit note creation, and unnecessary scrap escalation. Use 'quality inspection Hold' when waiting for test results!

Final milestone of Category 1! You have escorted the rejected pallet into the caged Quarantine Store, verified physical Red Tags, and stored it in the correct root-cause bay. For Rejected Return to Vendor what is the mandatory next digital status transition in JIRA as parts are put away in the NG area?
After rejected parts are put away in the Quarantine Storage cage, which status does the JIRA ticket transition to from 'QC Done: Fail'?

EXCELLENT WORK! After rejected parts are placed in the NG area, the JIRA status moves from 'QC Done: Fail' to 'Quality Failed'. Parts stay locked in blocked stock until the review board decides what to do. CONGRATULATIONS! Modules 1 to 7 are now 100% COMPLETE! Your Inbound & Quarantine Specialist Certificate is unlocked!

DIGITAL AUDIT ERROR! Never jump prematurely to 'Scrapped' or 'Returned to Vendor' before the Material Review Board convenes and signs off! The immediate status change upon physical put-away in the NG cage is strictly 'Quality Failed'!

Welcome to Category 2: Line Issuance & Order Picking at Ather AURIC Plant M002! On the vehicle assembly line, real-time VIN consumption triggers the MES system to auto-generate a digital Warehouse Picking Task on your handheld scanner. Before picking any parts, what critical information must the line feeder verify on the task screen?
How does the Line Feeder receive picking instructions, and what must be verified before proceeding?
Spot on! The line feeder must verify the exact Part Number, Bin Location, Model Variant, and Delivery Workstation on the scanner before touching any parts.
Warning! Never pick parts without checking the screen details. Guessing part numbers leads to assembling wrong variants on the line.

You have arrived at High-Rise Rack Aisle 3. Two adjacent bins (Bin A-07 and Bin A-08) hold similar wiring harness crates. On your handheld screen, the task points to Bin A-08, but the picking quantity field is locked and blank. Why does Ather hide the pick quantity until you scan the rack beam QR code?
Arrange the mandatory 4-step sequence a Line Feeder must follow when executing a picking task:

Flawless insight! This is called Blind Picking. Hiding the quantity forces the operator to physically locate and scan the correct bin QR code first, preventing habitual grabbing of wrong parts from adjacent bins!
Misunderstanding! Blind picking is not a software glitch. It is a deliberate error-proofing mechanism to stop workers from guessing and grabbing from the wrong shelf.
To hurry up, you load picked parts onto an empty trolley and push it to the line without scanning the trolley barcode. What is wrong?
Can the line feeder move un-scanned materials directly to the assembly line?

STOP IS THE ONLY ACTION! In Ather, every mobile trolley must be digitally married to the picking task by scanning the trolley QR code. Unmarried trolleys cannot be tracked, leading to misplaced inventory and assembly delays.
Strict violation! Never push an un-scanned trolley to the line. Without scanning the trolley QR, the system cannot verify if the right parts are heading to the right workstation.

You have arrived at Workstation 08 on the vehicle assembly line and offloaded the kitted wiring harnesses into the station rack. What two mandatory actions must you perform before leaving the workstation to ensure your delivery cycle is officially closed and shopfloor safety is maintained?
Inspect Workstation 08. Which two conditions violate Ather Line-Feeding and Shopfloor Safety rules?
Spot on! Scan the workstation destination QR code to confirm delivery and close the system task, then park the empty mobile trolley in the marked return lane so walkways remain clear.
Incomplete handover! Walking away without scanning the station QR leaves your task open in the system, and dumping the trolley in the pathway creates safety tripping hazards.

Attention Line Feeder! Your scanner screen calls for exactly 2 headlamp assemblies for Workstation 06. The supply crate holds 4 units. To save walking time on your next round, you decide to take all 4 headlamps right now. Is over-picking allowed?
The handheld scanner screen says 'Pick 12 pieces'. You see 15 on the rack bin. Take 15 to save a return trip?
OVER-PICKING STRICTLY FORBIDDEN! Pick only the exact quantity shown on the scanner. Extra parts congest workstation racks, risk cosmetic scratches, and cause false stockouts in the system!
Critical violation! Taking more parts than assigned creates ghost shortages in the warehouse and clutters the assembly line. Always follow the exact pick list quantity!

On a busy factory floor, two line feeders are working side by side. Feeder A is assigned to pick wiring harnesses, while Feeder B is picking instrument clusters. Feeder B gets delayed at the water cooler, so Feeder A decides to pick B's parts without logging into B's handheld terminal. What is wrong with this action?
Under Ather Plant can two line feeders carry the same part to the assembly line?

Severe accountability breach! Every pick must be performed by the operator assigned in the system under their own login. Cross-picking scrambles operator traceability and makes error investigation impossible!
Traceability violation! Never pick tasks assigned to another associate's ID. Each operator owns their assigned picks for 100% quality accountability.

A new trainee feeder stands in front of rack bin HRR-A-03-05. They scan the rack QR code with the handheld scanner, but the red error light flashes and the screen beeps: 'Invalid Location Scanned'. What should the feeder do?
You cannot see the picking quantity on the handheld terminal screen. Why?

Proper troubleshooting! Check the screen to verify if you are standing at the exact bin assigned. If correct, clean the lens/barcode label, reposition the scanner, and if it still fails, escalate to the Zone Leader.
Unsafe bypass! Never force parts from an unscannable bin or enter numbers manually without supervision. Always verify location and notify the Zone Leader.

A line feeder in a rush needs brake levers from Supermarket Lane 02. However, the aisle is tight, so the feeder grabs 10 lever boxes from adjacent Lane 03 without scanning the lane QR code and loads them onto the trolley. What happens?
You pick from the wrong supermarket lane without scanning the lane QR code. What happens?

Exact system impact! The original picking task remains OPEN in the system, while the wrong parts reach the line, risking assembling the wrong model of brake levers on scooters! Always scan the lane QR code before picking!
Critical misconception! The system does not fix wrong picks automatically. Picking without scanning creates assembly defects and line stoppage.

Final milestone of Module 8! You have mastered system triggers, blind-quantity reveals, trolley marriage, over-picking rules, and workstation deliveries. Arrange the complete 5-step picking sequence in its exact chronological order!
Arrange the 5 picking steps in the correct order:

PERFECT 5-STEP LIFECYCLE MASTERY! Scan source location QR, Pick shown quantity, Move to workstation, Scan destination QR, then Start the next WH task! Stage 8: Vehicle Line Issuance & Order Picking is 100% complete!
INCORRECT SEQUENCE! Remember: You must scan source location QR first to unlock quantity, pick parts, move to station, scan destination QR to close the task, and only then start the next task!

Welcome to Stage 9! At Ather AURIC Plant M002, metal body parts (like Mid-Frames, side brackets, and swingarm mounts) undergo ACED coating before painting. How are ACED metal parts handled to prevent parts mix-up?
How are ACED metal parts formatted in the storage area and distributed across line feeders?
Spot on! ACED metal parts are loaded into dedicated trolleys color-coded by model and matched to the workstation Kanban schedule.
Warning! Never mix different model parts in the same trolley. Model mix-ups cause major assembly failures in the paint shop.

In the Paint Shop Decanting Area, scooter body parts arrive from suppliers in massive Foldable Large Containers. How many pallet positions are allocated for each body part (like Tail Side Panels), and what is the exact trigger to call replenishment from the High-Rise Racks?
How many buffer pallet positions must the Decanting Zone Leader maintain for each body part (e. G. Tail Side Panels)?

Exact two-bin rule! Each body part has exactly 2 positions: 1 Active bin (being decanted) and 1 Buffer bin. When the active bin empties, scanning its empty Kanban triggers replenishment from the racks before the buffer runs out!
Inventory breakdown! Waiting until both bins are empty causes line stoppages. Staging more than 2 bins clutters the floor. Strictly follow the 2-bin system.

The decanting team opens a crate of Tail Side Panels holding 110 panels. The mobile trolley is built to hold exactly 30 panels. The operator loads 24 panels and wants to dispatch the partial trolley to avoid waiting for the final 6 panels. Should this be allowed or stopped?
Can the decanting operator dispatch a partially filled trolley (24/30 panels) to the paint line?

STOP IS THE ONLY DECISION! Trolleys must be filled to their exact capacity of 30 panels. Sending partial trolleys breaks the Kanban loop, starves the paint booth, and causes inventory counts to mismatch!
Violation! Partial trolleys violate batch delivery standards. Wait until all 30 slots are filled before dispatching to the line.

A forklift operator just dropped a crate at the decanting station. Upon opening, the decanting team discovers Tail Centre Panels instead of Tail Side Panels due to a wrong tag! What must the decanting operator do?
Arrange the 4 mandatory steps to recover from a wrong part delivery without locking SAP warehouse management system:
Immediate return! Do not open or decant the wrong parts. Notify the Zone Leader and have the reach-truck return the crate back to its proper high-rise rack location.
Severe quality risk! Staging wrong parts at decanting risks feeding wrong colored or shaped panels to the line. Halt and return immediately.
What is the core purpose of decanting in Ather manufacturing operations?
What is 'Decanting'?
Spot on! Decanting transfers parts from bulky supplier packaging into clean, specialized mobile trolleys designed for safe, scratch-free line feeding.
Misunderstanding! Decanting is not just unpacking. It is a controlled transfer into clean production trolleys.
A supplier crate holds 120 side panels. The mobile trolley capacity is 30 panels. How many full trolleys will this single supplier crate produce?
A brake Foldable Large Container contains 90 brakes. The trolley holds 30. How many full trolleys from one Foldable Large Container?
Exact math! 120 divided by 30 equals exactly 4 full trolleys. Zero partial batches remain!
Math error! 120 panels divided by 30 capacity equals exactly 4 full trolleys.
The assembly line is switching production from Series 450X to 450S. How does the decanting team handle part color and model transitions?
The production plan is 20 black + 10 red vehicles. How many WH tasks are generated in the WH order?
Flawless changeover! Clear out the previous model's trolleys completely, scan the new model Kanban barcode, and verify the paint color code before filling new trolleys.
Model mix hazard! Never start loading new model parts while old model parts remain in the decant buffer.
Who is officially responsible for replenishing and maintaining the supermarket flow racks in the paint shop area?
Who keeps the paint-shop supermarket rack for body parts filled?
Exact role clarity! The Decanting Zone Leader and designated decant team own the restocking and First-In First-Out rotation of the paint supermarket racks.
Role confusion! External truck drivers or general security do not manage internal factory supermarket racks. This duty belongs strictly to the Decanting team.
A line feeder has just delivered a mobile trolley of side panels to the paint booth. The trolley is now completely empty. Where must this empty trolley immediately be returned?
After feeding a body-part trolley in the paint shop, where does the empty trolley go?
CORRECT REVERSE FLOW! Return it to the Decanting Area immediately so it can be inspected, cleaned, and reloaded with the next production batch. Never block walkways with empty trolleys!
Safety hazard! Leaving empty trolleys under stairways or blocking walkways violates factory fire safety rules.
Final milestone of Module 9! A paint-shop task requests body panels from the supermarket rack. What physical unit of material do you move to the paint line?
A paint-shop WH task asks for a body part. What do you move to the paint-work line?

PERFECT OPERATIONAL MASTERY! The entire loaded trolley! Scan the rack QR to initiate, move the entire trolley to the workstation, and scan the destination QR to close the task. Stage 9 is now 100% complete!
Incorrect movement! Never carry loose plastic panels by hand — this causes scratches, drops, and defects. Always transport the whole specialized trolley!
A maintenance supervisor rushes to the counter asking for an urgent spare sensor. He says: 'The line is down, I will give the SAP reservation slip later.' What should you do?
Can indirect consumables or maintenance spares be physically issued based on a verbal request from a shop supervisor?
STOP IS CORRECT! Indirect materials directly impact plant operating expenses. Issuing items without an approved reservation creates ghost shortages and audit discrepancies.
Warning! Never issue consumables or spare parts based on verbal promises. Always require an approved SAP reservation before handing over stock.

The maintenance supervisor returns with an official reservation slip. What is the mandatory SAP Transaction Code (T-Code) used to reserve indirect materials, and which storage locations govern the transfer?
What is the SAP transaction code and storage location route for indirect maintenance spares?
Spot on! Transaction MB21 generates the reservation and moves inventory from Central Stores to the Plant Maintenance location, maintaining 100% digital trace.
Incorrect T-Code! Reserving plant consumables requires MB21 against valid department cost centers.

Inspect the printed Material Requisition Slip presented at the counter. Issuing materials under an incomplete slip causes expenses to be billed to the wrong department. What critical defect is missing on this slip?
Which critical field on this Material Requisition Slip violates and blocks stock issuance?
Defect spotted! The slip is missing the authorized Cost Center and Engineer signature. Materials can never be disbursed without an approved cost center.
Critical oversight! Issuing stock without a Cost Center scrambles budget tracking and causes billing errors between departments.
The slip is corrected and re-authorized. Now arrange the mandatory 4-step custody handover sequence in the correct chronological order!
Arrange the 4 standard operating procedure steps for issuing indirect maintenance spares into the correct chronological order.
Spot on! First verify slip details, second post the SAP transfer, third physically disburse items across the counter, and fourth collect the receiver's physical signature on the voucher.
Incorrect sequence! Always complete the digital system transfer before physically handing over goods across the counter.

An assembly technician comes to the Indirect Stores counter requesting steel-toe safety shoes and a company winter jacket. Instead of an approved JIRA ticket, they present a scrap of paper with an informal handwritten note from their team lead. Should you allow or halt this issuance?
An associate requests safety shoes and a jacket presenting only an informal handwritten note without a JIRA ticket. Allow or halt?

STOP IS STRICTLY REQUIRED! Safety shoes, winter jackets, and uniforms need an approved JIRA Ticket with Employee ID and size before you hand them out! General spares need an SAP reservation, but PPE requires HR or safety approval in JIRA. Handwritten slips are never accepted!
SECURITY BREACH! Handing out safety shoes and uniforms without JIRA tickets breaks HR asset tracking, bypasses company quota limits, and results in direct audit penalties!

Final milestone of Module 10! In Central Indirect Stores, the physical stock of critical synthetic motor grease has dropped below its Safety Stock Reorder Point (ROP). How does the Indirect Stores Executive initiate systemic replenishment to prevent plant-wide breakdown shortages?
When indirect consumables drop below Reorder Point (ROP) in the central warehouse, what is the mandatory SAP workflow to replenish stock?

PURCHASE REQUISITION MASTERY! The Indirect Stores Executive generates an official Purchase Requisition (PR) in SAP referencing the Material Master, approved Cost Center, and vendor contract! Stage 10: Indirect Material Handling is now 100% complete!

INCORRECT REPLENISHMENT WORKFLOW! Central stores cannot purchase materials with petty cash or verbally call outside shops. Official replenishment requires an authorized SAP Purchase Requisition against approved plant budgets!

Welcome to Stage 11: Production Inspection & Quality Part Issuance Report (Part Issuance Request)! At Ather Auric, non-standard material requests (for engineering testing, validation, and warranty repairs) must be raised via a formal JIRA Part Issuance Request ticket. These items are non-returnable and charged directly to a cost center. An R&D engineer arrives demanding 2 battery packs with a blank Budget ID on the ticket, saying: 'Give them now, I will update JIRA tomorrow.' Should you issue these batteries? STOP or GO?
Can warehouse personnel pick or issue materials when the JIRA Part Issuance Request ticket is missing a Budget ID?

Spot on! In Ather, non-standard material dispatches strictly require an authorized Budget ID and Cost Center in JIRA before warehouse release. Releasing untracked high-value batteries creates financial discrepancies and audit violations.
Warning! Never issue high-value inventory on verbal promises. Always verify an approved Budget ID in the system before issuing stock.

Now that the Budget ID is verified on ticket Part Issuance Request-AURIC-1042, the requester asks you to pick the materials immediately. However, the ticket requests 30 Brake Calipers worth ₹45,000. What two mandatory sign-offs are required before warehouse manpower is authorized to pick?
Match each emergency Part Issuance Request request ticket to its mandatory authorization authority
Spot on! Any material request exceeding ₹25,000 strictly requires formal dual sign-off from both the Department HOD and Finance before stock can be picked.
Warning! For materials valued over ₹25,000, team lead approval alone is insufficient. Both Department Head and Finance sign-offs are mandatory.

A fully authorized Part Issuance Request ticket for 5 replacement instrument clusters arrives in the warehouse dispatch queue at 4:15 PM on Friday afternoon. What is the mandatory dispatch schedule and warehouse handling rule?
How does the 4:00 PM daily cutoff determine Part Issuance Request outbound dispatch timelines?
Spot on! The warehouse dispatch cut-off is strictly 4:00 PM. Requests received after 4:00 PM are staged securely and dispatched on the next working business day (Monday morning).
Warning! Dispatches after the 4:00 PM cut-off are forbidden to prevent rushed packing, security lapses, and nighttime transit risks.

The 30 brake calipers have been picked, foam-packed, and staged for dispatch to an Inter-Branch Plant. Outbound Delivery and Post Goods Issue are posted in SAP. Before Security raises the boom barrier, what complete documentation kit must be verified?
What documentation kit is legally required to authorize outbound material gate exit?
Spot on! Security must verify the official Tax Invoice / Delivery Challan, Government E-Way Bill with QR code, and approved Plant Gate Pass before allowing the truck to exit.
Critical breach! Moving goods outside without a valid E-Way Bill and Delivery Challan results in immediate truck seizure and massive government tax fines.

Dispatch routing check! Part Issuance Requests travel to 3 different places: First, another area inside AURIC plant; Second, another Ather factory; or Third, an outside vendor. Match each destination to its required SOP action!
Match each Part Issuance Request destination to its mandatory operational action

PERFECT ROUTING MATCH! First, Same Location: Pick, pack, and consume directly against Budget ID. Second, IBC (Another Plant): Raise Stock Transport Order (STO Purchase Order) alongside picking. Third, Vendor: Consume against Budget ID, generate manual Delivery Challan, and dispatch! Zero compliance errors!
ROUTING MISMATCH! Inter-branch transfers strictly require an SAP STO Purchase Order, whereas outside vendor dispatches require a Delivery Challan. Review and try again!

Data Entry Operator & Logistics Specialist Challenge! In SAP Billing transaction VF01, creating the wrong document type for an outbound STO truck can trigger immediate GST seizure fines exceeding ₹5,00,000! Match billing document types ZSTO and ZGST to their mandatory tax applications!
In SAP billing transaction VF01, how are document types ZSTO and ZGST applied?

EXPERT TAX COMPLIANCE! ZSTO is strictly for intra-state tax-free stock transfers inside the same state (e.g. Maharashtra to Maharashtra); ZGST is strictly for taxable inter-state transfers to another state requiring an official Government e-Invoice with QR code!

TAX REGULATORY BREACH! Generating ZSTO for inter-state shipments bypasses integrated IGST reporting, leading to immediate truck detention at state borders. ZGST must be used for inter-state transfers!

Final milestone of Module 11! The Part Issuance Request shipment has been loaded into the transport carrier truck, inspected by Security, and departed through the plant gates. What final mandatory action closes the Part Issuance Request lifecycle?
The Part Issuance Request parts have been dispatched. What officially closes the Part Issuance Request process?

EXCELLENT AUDIT CLOSURE! Update transport details in JIRA, attach the signed delivery challan or lorry receipt, and close the ticket! Leaving tickets open creates stock mismatches and accounting delays. Module 11 is now 100% complete!
AUDIT RISK! Never leave a JIRA ticket open after material departs, and never delete tickets! You MUST attach the signed Lorry Receipt / Proof of Handover and transition status to 'Closed'!

Welcome to Stage 12: Reverse Logistics & Empty Bin Loading! While collecting returnable empty plastic totes and dunnage trays from the vehicle assembly line, operators must visually audit every container before stacking. Defective, cracked, or foreign-contaminated bins will damage parts or cause transit spills on the return truck to the supplier. Spot and tap the defective container in this lot before stacking!
Which returnable plastic container has physical damage or foreign contamination that prevents pallet stacking?
Spot on! Defective, broken, or contaminated bins must be separated and marked for repair or scrap so suppliers never pack good components into broken packaging.
Warning! Never mix cracked or contaminated crates with clean returnable packaging. Doing so damages fresh parts during supplier replenishment.

Now, the defective parts are kept in the NG area marked 'Quality Failed'. Normally, vendor defect parts are returned to vendor within 3 days. But the assembly line is running out of handlebar grip sleeves! Quality finds the defect is only a minor color shade difference. The Supplier Manager requests a 'Use As It Is' deviation in JIRA. Who alone can approve this deviation, and how is the stock moved back into SAP for assembly?
Line assembly is starved for handlebar sleeves with a minor cosmetic tint flaw. 4.4 & 4.5, what is the mandatory approval and SAP stock conversion sequence for a 'Use As It Is' deviation?

Spot on! Only the Head of Quality (SQA Head) holds the authority to approve a 'Use As It Is' deviation. Once digitally approved, the stock is systematically released from Blocked Stock into unrestricted stock for line assembly.
Warning! Warehouse operators and production supervisors cannot accept defective parts on their own. Only the Head of Quality can authorize deviations.

Now we address shop floor EHS safety and empty container circulation! As battery pack and vehicle assembly proceeds, empty Foldable Large Containers and plastic totes accumulate rapidly. What is the strict maximum stacking height limit for empty containers to prevent tip-over accidents?
Can an operator stack empty plastic bins higher than 5 feet (operator height) to conserve shop floor gangway space?
Spot on! Empty Foldable Large Containers have a strict maximum stacking limit of 5 containers high on level staging bays to prevent tipping hazards and protect walking associates.
Dangerous safety hazard! Stacking higher than 5 bins makes the stack unstable, risking serious crush injuries to shopfloor associates.

The final gate of Stage 12! An outbound supplier truck is parked at the dock ready to return empty containers to the vendor. What mandatory documentation and physical verification must occur before the driver departs?
Arrange the 4 standard operating procedure steps for reverse truck loading and factory gate clearance into the correct chronological order.
Spot on! Generate an authorized Delivery Challan in SAP detailing the exact container count and types, obtain the truck driver's signature on the receipt, and issue the Exit Gate Pass.
Warning! Never dispatch empty boxes without an official Delivery Challan and signed handover. Empty containers are company property and need strict audit tracking.

Urgent shopfloor safety audit! Along the main frame assembly line, an operator has emptied 6 plastic component totes and stacked them directly in the forklift gangway to clear station floor space. What is your mandatory action?
Empty trolleys and bins are left abandoned at the line side walkway. Allow or halt?

STOP IS ABSOLUTELY ESSENTIAL! Leaving empty bins in active gangways chokes forklift corridors, blocks emergency egress routes, and creates severe tripping hazards. Bins must be staged exclusively in designated yellow-marked line-side zones!
HAZARDOUS EHS VIOLATION! Abandoning empty bins on factory walkways creates tripping hazards, blocks emergency evacuations, and risks forklift collisions.

A supplier of defective mirror mounts was notified via JIRA with status 'To be Returned to Vendor' under the 3-day SLA. 72 hours have elapsed and the supplier has neither collected nor responded. What is the mandatory recovery action?
The supplier does not arrange pick-up of rejected Return to Vendor parts within 3 working days. What does the warehouse do?
STANDARD RECOVERY PROTOCOL! Dispatch the parts by commercial courier and debit the entire freight shipping and handling cost directly to the supplier's account via a formal debit note in SAP!
COST MISMANAGEMENT! Holding rejected parts forever chokes warehouse cage storage, while scrapping them at Ather's expense absorbs the supplier's fault. Courier with debit note is mandatory.
When a minor cosmetic flaw is accepted for production under a 'Use As Is' authorized deviation, arrange the 4 operational recovery steps in their exact sequence!
Put the 4 steps of the “Use As Is” deviation lifecycle into the exact correct sequence:

FLAWLESS DEVIATION FLOW! First, verify JIRA deviation approval; Second, move from Blocked Stock to Unrestricted in SAP; Third, remove Red Tag and apply Yellow Deviation Tag; Fourth, transfer to Supermarket racks!
DANGEROUS EXECUTION SEQUENCE! You must never move parts to supermarket racks while Red Tags are still affixed, and you must never disburse materials before SAP unblocks the lot!

An internal rework team has deburred and re-aligned 50 rejected wiring bracket subassemblies inside the factory workshop. The rework technician says: 'These are 100% fixed now, take them directly to the assembly line.' Should you permit or halt this line delivery?
Reworked parts come back from repair. Can they go straight to the assembly line?

HALT IS THE MANDATORY QUALITY DECISION! Reworked parts can NEVER enter production directly. They must be re-inspected 100% by quality inspection, cleared in JIRA, and carry an authorized green QC Pass stamp before assembly release!
SEVERE QUALITY HAZARD! Releasing reworked parts without QC re-inspection risks sending hidden defects into customer scooters. Always re-inspect 100%!

During internal assembly transit, 4 aluminum swingarms were dropped and severely bent by an in-house forklift operator. They cannot be reworked. What is the mandatory protocol to write off and scrap these non-supplier plant assets?
What is mandatory before non-supplier rejected parts are scrapped?

FINANCIAL INTEGRITY ENFORCED! Written approval from the Production Head and an official Plant Write-Off Voucher co-signed by Finance are mandatory before physically shredding internal scrapped assets!
UNAUTHORIZED DISPOSAL! Never scrap plant assets based on verbal comments. Scrapping company material requires signed functional and finance write-off vouchers.
Empty plastic bins collected from assembly lines have reached the central sorting yard. How must bins be staged before loading onto outbound supplier trucks?
How do you sort empty bins in the return area and route them to docked trucks?
DIGITAL LOGISTICS MASTERY! Sort by Supplier ID and Part Number in designated floor bays! Use the live visual dashboard to match staging inventory against truck arrival schedules.
LOGISTICS DISORGANIZATION! Piling all vendor bins into a random heap causes wrong containers to be sent to wrong suppliers, triggering packaging shortages across supply chains.
Urgent quality recall! Following a quality alert, a batch of 200 brake cables already in the supermarket racks must be recalled immediately. What urgent warehouse steps must you take?
A recalled lot of parts fails quality re-inspection. What happens under standard procedure?

RECALL ACTION COMPLETED! Stock is immediately moved to Blocked Stock in SAP. The warehouse team removes the whole lot from supermarket racks, puts Red Quarantine tags on every bin, and locks them inside the Quarantine cage!
CRITICAL SAFETY RISK! Recalled safety parts that fail re-inspection can NEVER return to unrestricted assembly stock. They must be quarantined and scrapped immediately.

GRANDMASTER CERTIFICATION MILESTONE! You have reached the 91st and final scene of the Ather AURIC Plant M002 Warehouse Training Program! Across 12 comprehensive modules, you mastered Inbound Docks, quality inspection Clearance, Put-Away, Battery Rooms, Hazardous Chemicals, Supermarkets, Quarantine, Order Picking, Paint Decanting, Indirect Stores, PIR Dispatches, and Reverse Logistics. What foundational principle governs every single action in our warehouse?
What core operational principle unites all 12 modules of the Ather AURIC Plant M002 Warehouse System?

CONGRATULATIONS, GRANDMASTER! Always remember the double-check rule: Every physical movement must match real-time system scans in SAP and JIRA. This ensures 100% vehicle traceability and zero defect leakage! You have completed all 91 Scenes across all 12 Modules with distinction! Your official Ather AURIC Grandmaster Certificate is now unlocked! View your certificate in the menu!
Never compromise on digital verification! Warehouse speed without system discipline causes line stoppages and defect leakage. Always marry physical handling to digital barcode scans!

Outstanding job, Operations Associate! Every delivery was verified, quality inspections were enforced, battery cells were safely vaulted, and the assembly line ran smoothly with zero defect downtime. You have mastered the Ather Auric warehouse standard operating procedures! Your shift is officially complete. Fantastic work!
